etymology_text: Of indeterminate origin, possibly a Wanderwort. First attested in the Hebrew of the Babylonian Talmud. Related to Jewish Babylonian Aramaic חֲתוּלָא, a plural form of which appears in the Targum Jonathan version of Isaiah 13:22, rendering the Hebrew אִיִּים (“jackals”) as חֲתוּלִין (“cats”). Compare also Arabic قط (qiṭṭ), Latin cattus.

head_templates.expansion: דֶּלֶת • (délet) f (dual indefinite דלתיים / דְּלָתַיִם, plural indefinite דְּלָתוֹת, singular construct דֶּלֶת־, plural construct דַּלְתוֹת־) [pattern: קֶטֶל]

etymology_text: From Proto-Semitic *dalt- (“door”), cognate with Akkadian 𒄑𒅅 (daltum), Ugaritic 𐎄𐎍𐎚 (dlt /⁠daltu⁠/), and Aramaic דַּלְתָּא. The /t/, which originally marked it as a feminine, has been reinterpreted as the third root consonant and the noun has taken the form of a segolate. Doublet of דָּלֶ״ת (dale"t, “dalet”)

examples.text: וּשְׁתַּיִם דְּלָתוֹת לַדְּלָתוֹת שְׁתַּיִם מוּסַבּוֹת דְּלָתוֹת שְׁתַּיִם לְדֶלֶת אֶחָת וּשְׁתֵּי דְלָתוֹת לָאַחֶרֶת׃
examples.ref: Tanach, Ezekiel 41:24, with translation of the Jewish Publication Society:
examples.english: And the doors had two leaves [apiece], two turning leaves; two leaves for the one door, and two leaves for the other.
examples.roman: U-shtáyim dlatót la-dlatót shtáyim musabot dlatót shtáyim l-délet eḥat u-shtéy dlatót la-aḥéret.
examples.translation: And the doors had two leaves [apiece], two turning leaves; two leaves for the one door, and two leaves for the other.

examples.text: וַיָּסֶךְ בִּדְלָתַיִם יָם בְּגִיחוֹ מֵרֶחֶם יֵצֵא׃
examples.ref: Tanach, Job 38:8, with translation of the Jewish Publication Society:
examples.english: Or who shut up the sea with doors, When it broke forth, and issued out of the womb
examples.roman: Va-yásekh bi-dlatáyim yam; b-giḥo me-réḥem yetsé
examples.translation: Or who shut up the sea with doors, When it broke forth, and issued out of the womb

examples.text: הַמַּשְׂכִּיר בַּיִת לַחֲבֵרוֹ, הַמַּשְׂכִּיר חַיָּב בַּדֶּלֶת, בַּנֶּגֶר, וּבְמַנְעוּל, וּבְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂה אֻמָּן.
examples.ref: a. 217 C.E., Mishnah. Bava Metzi'a, section 8.7:
examples.english: One who rents a house to his fellow, the landlord is obligated to provide the door, the bolt, and the lock, and any item which is made by a craftsman.
examples.roman: Ha-maskír báyit la-ḥaveró, ha-maskír ḥayyáv ba-délet, ba-néger, uva-man'úl, uv-khol davár she-ma'asé ummán.

examples.text: רָאָה שֶׁנִּנְעֲלָה דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי תִּינוֹק — שׁוֹבְרָהּ וּמוֹצִיאוֹ

head_templates.expansion: דיבר / דִּבֵּר • (dibér) (pi'el construction, future יְדַבֵּר, passive counterpart דובר / דֻּבַּר)

etymology_text: Compare Ugaritic 𐎄𐎁𐎗 (dbr, “to speak, say”).

examples.text: וַיִּחַר־אַף יְהוָה בְּמֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר הֲלֹא אַהֲרֹן אָחִיךָ הַלֵּוִי יָדַעְתִּי כִּי־דַבֵּר יְדַבֵּר הוּא וְגַם הִנֵּה־הוּא יֹצֵא לִקְרָאתֶךָ וְרָאֲךָ וְשָׂמַח בְּלִבּוֹ׃
examples.ref: Tanach, Exodus 4:14, with translation of the Jewish Publication Society:
examples.english: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and He said: ‘Is there not Aaron thy brother the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee; and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
examples.roman:
vayikhar-'áf YHVH b'moshé vayómer haló 'aharón 'akhíkha haleví yadá'ti ki-dabér y'dabér hú v'gám hine-hú yotsé likratékha v'ra'akhá v'samákh b'libó.
wayyiḥar-ʾap̄ YHWH bəmōše wayyṓmer hălō ʾahărōn ʾāḥī́ḵā hallēwī yāḏáʿtī kī-ḏabbēr yəḏabbēr hū wəḡam hinnē-hū yōṣē liqrāṯéḵā wərāʾăḵā wəśāmaḥ bəlibbō.
examples.translation: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and He said: ‘Is there not Aaron thy brother the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee; and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
